parts.note: not an exhibition of boats for sale but a public spectacle of boats racing on the water

explanation.definitionFit: Ravages are the damage or devastation left behind, so ruins in the sense of destruction.

explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Lake District, the region of Cumbria famous for walking.

definitions.meaning: the ... section, or a band of ... players
British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.definitionFit: Players of trumpets and trombones form a section named after the metal, which also means brazen nerve.

clue.text: Tardy but exciting tennis from the side

parts.note: late means tardy
a rally is an exciting long exchange of shots in tennis

explanation.surface: A player arrives late but a thrilling match is watched from the sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means to do with the side, so the adverb means sideways.

parts.words: Swinburne was up early, writing his
parts.note: Swinburne's collection of poems has a title saying they came before dawn, so 'up early' points to that title's first word

explanation.surface: The poet rose at dawn to write.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinburne's 1871 collection of lyrics was titled for pieces sung before dawn.

clue.text: Takes in with the eyes of a sailor

explanation.definitionFit: To soak up or assimilate something is to take it in.

explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'Sphere-born harmonious sisters, Voice and Verse'; the dash in the printed clue marks the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton pairs song and poetry as two sisters, the singing one being the human vocal sound.

clue.text: Gascony produces a snake with dangerous potential

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
stings are what make a creature dangerous

explanation.surface: A region of France turns out a serpent that could do harm.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons were proverbial braggarts, which is why bragging is called gasconade; so what Gascony produces is bluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascons had a name for bragging, so the region's typical output is bragging talk.

parts.note: a tutor riding in a vehicle, and also the name of a light two-wheeled carriage that shares a private tutor's title

explanation.surface: Someone is gleeful that the schoolmistress is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the cart' is British slang for in trouble; but a governess cart was a small two-wheeled trap with seats facing each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A private tutor for children at home shares her name with a small pony trap.

parts.note: the vertical board of a stair, and also someone who gets up, as an early one does

explanation.surface: A command to come forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The vertical part of each stair is called this; it is also one who rises, as in 'an early ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright face of a stair lifts the foot from tread to tread; someone who rises also goes up.

parts.note: not a hilltop with a good view but the mountain on which the Commandments were given to Moses

explanation.surface: A hill with a view over the land, the sort an army seizes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'commanding height' is military language for high ground; here it is the mountain of the Ten Commandments.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses received the Ten Commandments on this Biblical mountain.

parts.note: the language of the North Atlantic island stays closest of any living tongue to the speech of the Vikings

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a language as ancient Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the North Atlantic island has changed least from the Vikings' speech.

parts.note: wrapping a wire or a building so that heat or electricity cannot pass

explanation.walkthrough: Connexion is an old spelling of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagging or wrapping stops current or heat passing, isolating one side from the other.

indicators.note: the word change tells you the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A thin fabric imitating satin is a dress material.

parts.note: not trade union organisers of a slowdown but the animals that would naturally head any slow movement

explanation.surface: Union officials who called a work-to-rule.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a form of industrial protest; the slowest of creatures would be its natural leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelled reptiles are proverbially the slowest creatures.

explanation.surface: A line of Tennyson with two words missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line ends 'From precedent to precedent', both dashes taking the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: English liberty grows case by case, each earlier legal ruling guiding the next.

clue.text: Its last days were well booked

clue.text: It's not quite simple getting on to the under-pass

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine route has a famous railway tunnel running beneath the pass.

clue.text: Mother to a certain degree is a deadly type

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother with some qualification turns out to be lethal.
explanation.definitionFit: This African snake is one of the most venomous in the world.

definitions.meaning: ..., past tense of mope, to be listless and gloomy

clue.text: Dan's tempestuous appearance in the desert

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means advantageous or fit; as a noun, a stopgap means or contrivance.
